name: Northwest to British Columbia
why: Ties BPA to BC Hydro at the Canadian border. Power can flow either way.

name: West of Cascades North
why: Carries power from Grand Coulee and the other Columbia dams over the mountains to Seattle and Puget Sound.

name: West of Cascades South
why: Carries power from the Gorge west to Portland and the Willamette Valley. Most of the Gorge's wind, including Avangrid's, sits east of it.

name: Montana to Northwest
why: Brings power from Montana into the Northwest. The lines that define it are farther east in Montana and Idaho; the badge marks where it heads into the map.

name: Idaho to Northwest
why: Ties the Northwest to Idaho. Includes the 500 kV line from Hemingway in Idaho to Summer Lake in Oregon.

name: Pacific DC Intertie
why: Sends Columbia power 846 miles to Sylmar near Los Angeles. It's DC and has no stops along the way.

name: California-Oregon Intertie
why: Three 500 kV AC lines from southern Oregon into Northern California: two from Malin to Round Mountain and one from Captain Jack to Olinda.
